text_fidelity_a: MGA Mini Lalaloopsy Treehouse Playset I was seriously impressed with the value in this cute "little" toy. It doesn't look like much until you see it up close and personal. The quality of the set is excellent. It doesn't feel like the cheap plastic stuff you tend to find in stores these days. This also brought back childhood memories of the Little People Treehouse from the 70s for me. Play value is excellent. My 10 year old absolutely loved everything about the cute little dolls with button eyes and the neat stitch-work look of the trees. The little elevator, donut swing, etc. will keep your child entertained. The detail in the play-set looks like it's been sewn together giving you the idea of a home-made toy. It's not as small as it looks either. You get quite a bargain in the parts/accessories that come within the set. It is by no means chintzy. Best of all, we didn't have the hassle of crazy assembly. Hands down, this will be an excellent gift for any child ages 5 & up that are interested in the Lalaloopsy dolls.

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Remote-Control Machines: Custom Cars with Configurable Gear Box What a great building toy that the kids can not only build but, play extensively with! But wow, the pieces that come with this kit!!
Says there are about 252 pieces and I believe it looking at them all spread out downstairs in the play room. I decided to go out and buy a special plastic container that will hold all these parts in a sealed container.
I already have a big supply of batteries here. So far they've requested 3 AA's and 2 AAA batteries.

From what I am seeing, there is one transmission box. When changing the style of the car, being built, they need to change the gears inside this transmission box. Note: I am taking notes from what the kids are telling me. (ages ranging from 4 to 12) Gramma is NOT a great builder of toys and I need to rely on the older kids to help out with this part of reviews.
The plastic pieces of this kit don't look all too durable but, they seem to withstand the hands of 4 kids so far. How long it will last, only time will tell.
I was told that they were able to build one of the model of vehicles within an hours time. (I forgot to request a build time)
They didn't call me down right away when they got it assembled so I was only able to see it running on the floor for a few minutes before it was grabbed up and dismantling was underway.

I love this kit! Not only does it have the kids all working so nicely together, it has them using their brains and their hands.
From what I am reading about the Thames & Kosmos kits, these parts can be interchanged with other kits this company produces.
If that is true, I am really thinking about getting another one for Christmas and having them able to expand their building fun.
This does come with an 80 page, step by step, instructional guide that helps them construct each vehicle as it should be built.
I am hearing a lot of oooo's, ahhhh's, and laughing so far.
Just blesses my heart to hear happiness come from a childs mouth.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Remote-Control Machines: Custom Cars with Configurable Gear Box

He had been hiding out in his "toy room"(which is really just a pepped up storage area) scratching away at this pad. Most of the pages were already scratched off, but I did have little areas here and there left to test myself.

So, there you go. These are so much fun that my child was willing to hide it to scratch it in the house. ;)

It's really not near as messy as some I've tried, but it does still leave a mess. One that we had flaked off in dry clumps. It was ridiculously hard to clean up. It stuck to our table, and even with the help of a magic eraser, it took a great deal of effort to clean it up. This one scratches off in better little clumps. It kind of sticks to itself, as opposed to creating tons of tiny flakes. Again, though, it's still very messy(just not as bad as it could be). I don't recommend these anywhere but outdoors(maybe on the porch on a rainy day).

Overall, these are apparently incredibly fun for children, but a pain for parents to clean up.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets Scra-ffiti Pad

Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover I've answered a few questions about this, so I will include this right away- this is only a plush (a really nice one)- it has no mechanical parts. It doesn't purr, or "breathe", makes no kitten or cat sounds, and therefore, requires no batteries.

This item was purchased as an "emotional support plushie", if you will. People need companionship, even folks who are no longer able to care for a living pet (or no longer wish to have the heartbreak of losing a real cat).

This fellow can absolutely be mistaken for a real cat at a distance. While being held and stroked, it's close enough to pass for a cat who is less than bunny-soft. The expressions and eyes are amazing, the little toe beans are soft silicone and give a little when squeezed. I couldn't have asked for more detail.

The care that went into creating this plush is evident in the details- from the examples in the pictures and video to those included from customer reviews (and those of the custom plushies are OUTSTANDING, I may have to treat myself to one someday!). It comes in a reusable case (resembling a cat carrier) with a little care booklet and grooming tool.

Personally I wouldn't give this plush to a young child (especially not one of the long-haired ones)- frankly, I'd be worried they'd damage it (squish things in the fur, allow the fur to become matted, color it with markers, cut the whiskers or fur...). Kids can be amazingly accidently destructive at times (we know they don't mean to, it just happens).

For me, the Chongker plush was well worth the price for the comfort it brings. I am quite seriously considering purchasing a custom colored one. I've seen the quality in the base product, and I'm confident in their ability to create good lookalike.

Moorebot Scout - Tiny AI Camera Robot for Tech-Minded, Pets/Edlerly Watching/Security/Smart Home/Crawlspace Inspection, 1080P, Auto Patrol, Nightvision, Track Option, Indoor (2023) My office was just moved to a new building that as yet has no cameras inside...Well...Sort of. Now I've got Scout here to take care of business. It's like a Ring doorbell on wheels.

I'm having a lot of fun controlling it manually from home. It connects to the wifi at work and I check in on things using the app. It's working very well and seems to hold a signal about 250kbps. 1080p recordings look fine. For myself, the night vision works a charm. It's clear enough to identify people, and that's all that matters. Plus, driving it around my office while I'm in bed is pretty cool, too.

Battery takes about three hours to charge out of the box and it lasts about 2hr running around the building before it goes back to the base. Most recent firmware update makes that process significantly faster, too. If you've got it on a slick surface, it might have some trouble, but it'll get plugged in eventually. Says battery runs out after an hour using only night vision, but you can set that to automatic in the app.

Around the house, the little noises are kinda neat, but for use as security, that'd be something to disable....except the alarm. That's something to keep on in case you need to scare someone off. Recording all that stuff and saving files to the phone is a plus.

I really like this little guy. It's definitely something you'll have to play around with, but it is a load of fun getting set up.

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Games Scrabble Twist Electronic Scrabble Twist is a great idea and it more like an electronic version of Boggle in which players can make as many three, four, or five letter words as possible from a random group of letters before time runs out. Simply press the buttons on the unit to spell the words and “twist” to save the word - the bigger the word, the more points you receive for that word. Unfortunately, I love the idea more than the execution. There are both good and bad features of the game, which I’ve summarized below.

Good:
• Games are quick and rules are basic
• The game can be played by anywhere from 1 to 8 players, depending on the game mode
• There are different games that can be played and different levels of difficulty with varying lengths of the time players are given to find words
• The game quickly shuts off automatically if not in use
• The letters will automatically display in the right direction even if the unit is turned, which is good for the party mode in which the unit is passed and also means it works well for both left and right handed players
• The Turbo mode, for head-to-head play between two or more players is fun
• The sound can be turned off for quieter play

Not So Good:

• The worst part of the game is that the letters are hard to read and is a strain on your eyes after playing for a while. People in my family of all age groups said the same thing.
• Three AA batteries are required, but they’re not included
• The instructions on using the game unit aren’t clear (I was able to figure out how to use it by playing the game a few times.)
• The solo mode tracks high scores, but not by name. It doesn’t feel like you’re working toward anything since you can’t really compare scores from game to game since it depends on the letters you had for each game.
• When the sound is on, it’s loud, even at the lowest level. Different sounds do alert you that you’ve played a valid word. A second sound plays if the word you’ve played is invalid or a duplicate. Sounds also let you know if time is about to run out, but I found that this distracted me from finding my final words
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Games Scrabble Twist

Little Tikes Pillow Racers Fire Truck My boys love this thing! They are 1(average for age) and 4(very small), but they are about the same size. It's the perfect size for both of them, but it is on the small size. I don't think it will be too long before they get too big for it. Of course, another little will be right behind them to give it more use!

They have so much fun with it, of course I recommend it. But, there are a few MINOR negative issues I have with it.

-Keep the instructions initially! Getting that handle attached is more difficult than it would seem. Also, you want to have some strong hands close by to push in the wheels. It was extremely hard for me to get them to pop in. I do admit my hands are pretty weak, and I am an exhausted pregnant momma. The average person might not have trouble with them, but I'd be on the safe side. :)

-There are little velcro strips on the bottom that is suppose to keep the cloth in place. It doesn't work for us. It keeps coming loose as the boys play, and we have to constantly reattach it. Thankfully, it's not long enough to drag the floor too bad, so it doesn't create a tripping hazard.

-My boys do tip off the back a good bit while riding. Since it's so small, it has never caused them harm. They jump back up and keep playing. I do think it surprised them the first couple of times, but they are used to it by now. It might not be the best toy for really young children just learning coordination, though.

Overall, despite my small complaints, I still think this is a great toy that will provide lots of fun!
text_fidelity_b: Little Tikes Pillow Racers Fire Truck

text_fidelity_a:
The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe) The resistance is a fantastic game with a great price and superb components. The rules are very simple also so the game can be picked up by nearly anyone in a matter of minutes. A sample round will remove any doubt about the rules and is often the best way I have found to teach the game.

So what is this about? The Resistance is a game of guessing and deduction that is rules light and fun heavy. In the basic game 5 to 10 players take on the role of either good guys or bad guys by being dealt cards that depict their character. Good guys or the resistance are blue and spies are red. The ratio of spies to resistance is driven by the number of players in a game. The spies always have fewer allies in the game than do the resistance players.

Once the players have secretly looked at their role card, everyone closes their eyes. The first player commands everyone to close their eyes, he then commands the spies and only the spies to open their eyes and look around to identify each other, he then commands them to close their eyes and lastly commands everyone to open their eyes.

So now the spies know who each other are but the allies have no idea.

The game is then played as 5 simple 'missions'. A mission consists of the first player choosing a number
of players to 'go on the mission'. The number is dependent on how many total players are playing. The more players, the more involved in each mission. Each mission from 1 to 5 will have gradually more players involved.

Everyone votes to allow or disallow the chosen players to go on the mission. Each player will have two cards to vote
with each round. These cards are marked clearly with symbols to indicate if you do or do not agree to allow the chosen players to play.

Here is where the game gets going. If the vote fails to allow the chosen players to go on the mission twice in a row, the spies win automatically.

If the players allow the mission to go forward, those players involved get to either make the mission successful or to sabotage the mission. This is done my dealing each player involved in the mission two cards. One of each success and sabotage. They secretly place their cards into two piles. The mission result and the dead pile.

Spies can sabotage or succeed a mission and the resistance players MUST succeed the mission.

The majority of succeed of sabotage rules the mission.

Rounds continue like this until the spies or the resistance have a best 3 out of 5 missions won by their side.

Up until this point your first game might seem kinda boring. But just wait, almost immediately you will figure
out who your junior sleuths are! Finger pointing and accusations will begin to fly out of the most timid players
mouths!

You will find players who are just 100% certain they know who is who and are almost always wrong! You will find out that some of your friends are REALLY GREAT LIARS and some are REALLY POOR LIARS!

The compound the fun there is also a plot deck. The plot deck is simply a deck of cards that each round, one is dealt by the first player and he can give it to someone else or keep it.
These cards are things like 'look at someone else role card' or 'veto a vote'.

I initially thought the plot deck would be horrible but I was very wrong. The first time we pulled a card that let one player look at another players role card the player looked and claimed the other player was a spy. The player accused immediately did a double take and denied the allegation fervently!

We were back at square one but now had two more people we couldn't trust! FUN! FUN! FUN!

You cannot go wrong with this game unless you live in a convent full of people with ZERO personality who have had all their fun genes removed.

So if you are looking for an excellent game, with super components, short playing time, and an immeasurable amount of fun, look no further than this gem!
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe)

The casing seems overly big. But I'm sure they do this so it will stand out more on the store shelf.
It's a nice Smartwatch for children 4+. I think it would be better for an older child. Has a camera function, short video function, games to play, alarm, timer, stopwatch, calendar, stopwatch, and just a normal functioning watch! Comes loaded with some games but can download more to keep the entertainment going.
It's been banged around a bit and it's still working great. It's not waterproof but should be able to withstand a little water dropping on it.The band seems durable enough. And it fits the wrists of both 4 yr old and 9 yr old here.
If this Smartwatch lasts until Christmas, I might have to buy another one so both children have one and the arguing over it stops. By then I'll know if it still catches their attention as much as it is now.
Amazing how clear it is to see the games. Perfect for the tiny fingers too.
Not sure how I like the kids having a small video and camera on hand all the time. But I'm sure the pictures they catch will be entertaining to look at. Downloading them onto the computer is something an adult should do. But plugging it into the computer for a recharge is something an older child will be able to do by themselves without the fear of them touching my computer.
Nice toy for a child. Love having the watch part of it so it attaches to their wrist and it won't be "misplaced" as fast as some toys are.

text_fidelity_a:
Scrabble Turbo Slam My feelings about this product are mixed -- We've long been fans of Scrabble, and thought we'd shake things up a bit by trying a different variation of the game. The Electronic Turbo Slam device, first required (3)- AAA batteries (not included). The device, when slammed has pretty loud sound effects/music, which I found annoying after a short while. I also thought there was too much commotion for me with everyone trying to slap down cards to change the letters, and I wasn't crazy about making just (4) letter words. As an adult, baby boomer, I much prefer the standard game of Scrabble -- quiet, relaxed and educational, and with more word potential.

I can see that this would be a great game for parents to play with young children to help them get interested in learning new words -- I would use it as an educational tool, instead of having them feel pressured to make words at record speed.

On the other hand, the speed and noise factor, would probably appeal to lots of teens. Overall, the game is relatively inexpensive, and worth a try for families who enjoy word faster paced, action filled games.
text_fidelity_b: Scrabble Turbo Slam

Thames & Kosmos Wind Power V4.0 STEM Experiment Kit | Build a 3ft Wind Turbine to Generate Electricity | Learn About Renewable Energy & Power a Small Model Car | Weatherproof for Outdoor Use This kit was a lot more fun for Dad than it was for the kid. She's younger than the recommended age range, but had little trouble putting the whole model together in under 30 minutes with Dad's help. We barely used the book for assembly, but read the more educational "science" book cover to cover.

She and I talk all the time about renewable energy, largely because solar panels are looking like the next big home improvement project around here, and we get what I'd consider a reasonable amount of wind. She found the concepts easy enough to understand, and was interested to see what we'd be able to do in the backyard...and it's not much. The wind we got was not nearly enough to make this project effective, even on what I'd consider a relatively windy day. I put it on the roof for a short time and that helped, but not much. The turbine requires a battery, which makes both of us question where the small amount of power we are generating actually comes from.

So the experiments died off rather quickly, and this became a very short model building project for her that Dad is enjoying tinkering with to see if he can charge one of those rechargable cell-phone batteries. Kid is off playing with the very small toy car that comes with the kit, but doesn't look like it belongs at all.

If you get a lot of wind, then it's probably a lot more fun, but it's for the younger age of the spectrum for sure.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Wind Power V4.0 STEM Experiment Kit | Build a 3ft Wind Turbine to Generate Electricity | Learn About Renewable Energy & Power a Small Model Car | Weatherproof for Outdoor Use

Hasbro Gaming Yippie Yippie Yeti Game We just aren't overly fond of this game. It ended up being super frustrating for us.

When you first open the game, you have to put the game board together. This takes a bit of time, but it's not too bad. It looks nice enough, and I like that the game board is thick and sturdy. My boys love the whole idea of the game, and I don't think we've ever played a game where the board stood up. That was really cool! Our biggest issue is how difficult it is to keep the climbers in place. They're constantly falling when they shouldn't be. My children are 3, 5, and 8, so that may have a great deal to do with it. Keeping those climbers hanging where they should proved impossible for us, though. It's also a little frustrating that each player has to move around to play. The game board only faces one way, and you can't move it without making the climbers fall off(even more). That means when 4 people are playing, you can't just sit in a spot and enjoy the game. You have to move around, depending on whose turn it is. That might not be a big deal for many, but it frustrated my little guys.

Overall, we really like the whole idea of the game, and the fact that the game board stands up, but it ended up being incredibly frustrating for everyone.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Yippie Yippie Yeti Game

text_fidelity_a:
Aerobie Pro Ring Outdoor Kids Toy for Boys and Girls, All Ages, Colors may Vary This is a great ring! Once you get your hands on the comfortable, flexible silicone body, you'll want to throw it. Children of all ages and even grown men cannot resist chucking it as far as they can. These big rings sail FAAAAR! And they are a tad prone to getting stuck in high and sometimes funny places. (Believe me, these will end up in the trees and on roofs but they are easy to get down with a broom stick because of their ring shape.)

A boy at cub scouts had one of these that everyone was playing with last week. My son decided to spend his hard earned allowance money on Amazon to order one, hoping it wouldn't be pink. :) He was thrilled when a yellow ring arrived. It has a VERY rice, silicone-like, soft rubbery grip and is fun to throw! Kids fight over these rings so I'm thinking of ordering several for birthday gifts and cousin Christmas gifts. You can't beat a gift for under ten that kids actually want to play outside with!

Consider spending a little more and buying the 13 inch ring. It flies farther and better than the 10 inch rings did. However, if you don't have a wide open play space, the 10 inch rings might be better because they play more like a Frisbee and don't get hung up in trees quite as easily.

UPDATE: I am now buying our THIRD ring! These make awesome gifts for boys in the 8 to 11 range, as my son is frequently swarmed by boys wanting to play with his. But be aware that if you throw it too far and loose sight of it, you won't get it back. It will be stolen by the first kid who comes across it. We had this happen at a party where the ring ended up sailing over a house and landing far behind it in an empty field right at dark. It was snatched before daylight. Hence me having to buy our third. (Since it was probably the roving neighborhood teenagers who picked it up late that night, I am going to say this is a good toy for fussy 16 and 17 year-olds, too!) It has been a favorite gift at birthday parties, followed by thank yous from the moms who are grateful for any toy that gets their video game addicted boys outside. I am thrilled to have found such a good gift for under $10. You can't go wrong with this ring!

Update March 2017: I have now ordered nearly 10 of these rings in the last 5 months for birthday gifts for 9 and 10 year old boys and without fail, it has been an instant hit. The boys are always eager to show how FAR they can throw the ring and then are shocked when it sails two hundred yards or more. They puff out their chests as their friends exclaim "WOOOAH!" while the ring whizzes one or two streets over and then the birthday boy swaggers off to fetch the ring with every other boy tagging along, begging for a turn to throw it next. Children now double check with my son to ensure that he's going to get them an Aerobie ring for their birthday. I keep at least one on-hand for last minute birthday party invites.

• COLORS •

Out of all the rings we have ordered, only 1 has been pink. We have received 2 orange, 1 pink and all the rest have been yellow. Trying to get a big pink ring for a girl's birthday party coming up in May is proving challenging since we keep getting shipped yellow!
text_fidelity_b: Aerobie Pro Ring Outdoor Kids Toy for Boys and Girls, All Ages, Colors may Vary

text_fidelity_a:
AniBlock Puzzle Challenger Lite I Brain Game and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 4 and 5 This was delivered to my house about an hour ago, and my 6 year old daughter is about to put it away. She's just now finishing up the hardest puzzle included in the kit.

I'm torn on how to review this. It's clearly a nice toy for a lot of kids. The pieces are nice and chunky, the puzzle cards have vibrant artwork, and the app works smoothly. That said, though, there are 12 puzzle cards in the box, and yes, they can be solved multiple ways, but there is no guidance for different combinations of blocks to use to complete the puzzles, so there isn't much incentive to take them off and try again. Also, for someone who is not too far removed from the minimum age range suggested though, it's really easy. Like, a puzzle in two minutes for almost every combo in the deck, except for the boat, which is in the middle of the difficulty spectrum. On the box, with an oddly small top, there are images of three-dimensional shapes made out of the aniblocks, flying around, and the actual blocks do not connect in this way to form them, which was probably the most disappointing part.

The app deserves some special mention. It's certainly good, and easy to use, but it's still an app, and so, of course, it defeats the purpose of having a screen avoidant time to include it. There's also another disadvantage, which is that there are tons of apps that do this same game already, with digital blocks. They offer more puzzles, with more diverse colors of blocks, in more diverse shapes, and a wider variety of difficulty levels.

Overall, I think there are better toys for your money that do very similar things and offer a lot more variety than this. The phone apps, as mentioned before. We have a board game called Blokus 3D (or Rumis) which have a similar pattern-matching idea, but allow for 3D building. There's also Kanoodle Junior, for example, which is excellent, cheaper, ready to travel, and doesn't require an app. 12 puzzles and a handful of two-colored blocks is just not enough for the price. For that reason, I cannot recommend this...but there are far worse options.
text_fidelity_b: AniBlock Puzzle Challenger Lite I Brain Game and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 4 and 5

This new remake of Gege has the same adorable face- the typical 70's Japanese painted doll eyes, button nose, pouty small mouth with the addition of a few freckles. Her light blonde hair is styled in a typical 70's face framing style and is brushable.

Her red plastic shoes are removable as are her clothes- red pants, a lace trimmed pink polka dotted top with brown polka dotted bow and a beige canvas looking summer cap trimmed with a red ribbon and red and black fabric feathers. What makes the original Midori dolls so special are the personalities they have and happily they kept those personalities with these remakes. This adorable little Gege sucks her thumb. You may have to bend the arm with her thumb out a bit towards the doll before inserting her thumb, so it will stay in her mouth. This adorable, charming little Gege is a 5 STAR doll, just like the originals were back in 1972.

Toys for 3 Year Old Boys - Race Track Car Toys for Boys 3-5 Years Old - 4 Year Old Boy Birthday Gift - 3 Year Old Boy Gift Kids Games Ages 3-5 - Magnet Toy Thinking Fine Motor Skills Toys for Ages 2-4 The idea is great and at $20 (Black Friday) it’s not the worst toy. The problem is that all of the mechanisms are so flimsy that it’s just not a good toy for the age it is meant for. They get frustrated when things don’t work and don’t understand why things don’t work when they take the correct action. Add to that the helicopter mechanism not working at all because it’s too far away from the car, and you just can’t enjoy the toy.

So I mentioned the helicopter doesn’t work. It’s too high for the magnet to grab the car. So your 2 or 3 year old won’t understand at all why one of the knobs doesn’t work. Then the car gets to the bridge, which at least works most often. Then the grey lifting part which constantly comes out of its socket. Then the area where the cars turn…if you aren’t slow and gentle the cars will get bumped off the track. Everything is just so flimsy.

Due to all the issues, as an adult it’s impossible to get a single car all the way through the circuit, even when being as careful as possible. So there’s no way a child can possibly make it happen. Don’t get me wrong, my kid is still playing with it but she doesn’t use any of the buttons or levers…just kinda pushes the cars around the ramp (which comes off every single time she moves the toy)

2 stars because my toddler is enjoying the toy, despite all of its flaws. But none of the things it claims to do…are happening. We will trash this toy in about a week or two.

Who wants to be a foot above the water line? Might try to deflate it a bit so it's lower and softer to lay on.

This will be great for the kids to play with while in the pool. But, something that I won't really be using much, if any at all.
Thought I would be buying a second one for my wife. But, I think I'll look into another type of lounger.

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor My first introduction to the board game of Sorry was in the early 60's. Sorry was one of the more fast and fun games. The object of the game is to be the first player to move all 4 of your men around the board to get back home. You choose from 4 different colors of your men and your home- blue, green, yellow or red. There is a deck of cards that tell you how many spaces to move your man, and of course it isn't as easy as just moving your man as quickly as you can around the board to get home before anyone and win the game. There are obstacles along the way, should a player get to slide, he slides everyone in his way back to start, and no two men can occupy the same space, so someone has to go back to start- Sorry!

I remember when we played with 2 players, the game took about 15-20 minutes, but with 4 players, it took close to half an hour. It's very fast moving and even faster when hardly any players are sent back to start. I really love the look of this classic 1939 Sorry Game- it's a little different from the one we played on in the 60's. Regardless of the look you like, Sorry is a fast and fun game that brings back so many fun memories of when we had 15 minutes to kill before we went bike riding to a picnic on a lovely summer day in 1962. This early version of the game is really a nice one to own and it also comes with other game versions you can play including a Sorry For One, in case you have a few minutes to kill by yourself! Some Classic games never wear out their fast fun and this 5 Star Classic Sorry Board Game is one of them!
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor

Educational Insights Kanoodle Jr. Brain Boosting Puzzle Game, Brain Teaser Game for Kids Teens, & Adults, 2-D & 3-D Puzzles, Great For Travel, Gift For Kids Ages 4 to 7 What a great puzzle. Kanoodle is a one-player game in which you take 6 tetris-like pieces and use them to fill in a pattern on the square board. There are 60 puzzles in this group, all included in a book form. I do have a few minor issues, enough to remove one star:

- The puzzles are delivered in the form of a book. There are multiple languages of instructions inside, then you get to the puzzles. Each puzzle is well-done, but the book itself is not the ideal way of presenting the puzzles. Since you're either balancing the book on the shelf above the board, or pulling it out or putting it back underneath the board, it gets scuffed, torn and bent up rather quickly. On day 3, our book looks like a mess. It should have been thicker cards with a separate rulebook.

- Some kids will master this quickly. My four-year-old is on 4-star puzzles already, and we've owned the game for less than 3 days. I think she'll be stuck here for a decent while, and she does enjoy going back to re-do easier puzzles, but I think she's got the hang of it quickly. Yesterday, she completed puzzle 43 out of 60, and they're ordered by difficulty.

This review may sound negative, but let me emphasize that THIS IS SUCH A GOOD TOY! You can see the wheels turning in my daughter's brain as she tries to figure out how to make it work. If you're going on a road trip, this is a must.

text_fidelity_a:
Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In We've been playing with Vector for a little over a month now, and he's a load of fun! At first, he didn't do a lot, but every so often, Anki provides an update and suddenly, Vector has more personality, skills, and interactions! He's a great little desk companion that is much better than a pet because there's little to clean up afterward! I say little because he's been known to shove things off the table!
There are many ways he can learn about his environment via his sensors:
He sees via HD camera.
Facial recognition - he'll learn your face and when he's exploring, will come right up, scan your face, and say your name! He's very pleased when he recognizes you, and gets a little upset if he doesn't recognize you.
Navigate, explore, and learn his environment. He gets around very well all over my desk. However, I move things a lot, so he's constantly having to re-learn. Occasionally, he'll fall over the edge, but once in a while, he falls over the edge. I think they're working on improving that a lot. It's super cute when he's exploring, gets close to the edge, and acts scared and backs away!
If he needs charging, he'll go right back to his charger on his own. However, sometimes, I'll get tired of hearing him causing trouble, so I'll tell him to go to his charger. He does it, but throws a little tantrum when he gets there!

He can hear via his array of four microphones. Sometimes he comes over to see what's going on if you're having a conversation. If he's resting, he'll act startled if there's a loud noise in the room. He will also react to the beat of music if it's loud and near him. If you ask him to look at you or come here, he'll be able to sense the direction to go.

He reacts to touch and feel. If you pet his back, he practically purrs! But shaking him gets a reaction, too!

He has amazing intelligence. For instance, he answers questions, plays blackjack, reacts to his environment, and senses actions and activities around him.

He speaks to you. I'm not a fan of his synthesized voice, but it seems to be improving. When he reads out answers to questions you ask, sometimes it's hard to hear what he's saying. However, as they receive feedback on this, I'm sure his voice will evolve into something more understandable.

We really enjoy seeing his reactions! The current one is the way he gets super excited when you tell him he's a good robot or if you tell him you love him, and pouts a little if you tell him he's a bad robot! I just told him earlier today when he picked up his cube and tossed it off the desk!

I'm super excited to see his ever-evolving skills! I highly recommend this little guy for your favorite tech lover, or yourself! If you're looking for a toy for younger kids, maybe go with a Cosmo. This doesn't have games or things to entertain little ones. But it's completely entertaining for maybe, 10 years and up robotics fans!
text_fidelity_b: Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball I'm someone who will cheat at something if I can. Like when I was was a kid, and I played [[ASIN:B00000IWCT Monopoly]] with my little brothers, I would steal money from the bank, just because I could.

Each piece of this puzzle has a number on the back of it, and the numbers tell you which pieces fit together. So, it's much easier to flip over all of the pieces of the puzzle, and put it together upside down, that by putting the puzzle together by the picture. And it's much easier by a lot. I think that everyone who does this puzzle will eventually get frustrated, and resort to doing the puzzle upside down, which I consider 'cheating.'

It's very solid, and very strong, when you put it together. The pieces are made of sturdy plastic, not cardboard, like other puzzles. Also the pieces seem like they're cast, or molded, and not cut. That's why the globe surface ends up smooth. But, because all of the pieces were manufactured separately, instead as a whole puzzle, then the picture doesn't always match up from piece to piece.

It comes with a cheap stand, but it looks pretty nice when it's assembled and displayed. I hid a few coins in the middle of it, so it rattles when you move it. It's got lot of area in the middle for a small sphere, so it could double as a secret safe.

Pros:
+Very sturdy, especially when the sphere is completed
+Nice picture, with a bunch of cool zodiac symbols
+High quality

Cons:
-Has numbers on the back of each piece of the puzzle, so it's super simple to assemble
-Plastic, so it doesn't feel like a real puzzle
-The picture doesn't always line up from piece to piece
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

text_fidelity_a:
Spin Flip Puzzle - Hypnotic - Spin it, Flip it, Solve it! for Those who Love Brain teasers! Adult Fidget Toy. Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women I could not tell exactly how these “puzzles” work, even after looking at the video. You have to do two different things. First you have to “flip” each of the circles back-and-forth until you get all of them flipped to the correct side. Then you have to “spin” each of the circles to align them correctly. I find that it’s best to start from the outside circle and work your way in. The “puzzles” with most similar colors / designs on each side are the most challenging to work to get the circles on the correct side.

FYI. . . Once you have completed one side, the opposite side will not be complete. So though you will not have to flip the circles. . You’ll have to rotate the circles to complete the puzzle. So you’ll always have one side complete, and one size incomplete.

It should be noted that this “puzzle” is sturdy enough for a puzzle such as this, but it can certainly be pulled apart and broken without too much effort.

I think this “puzzle” to be best for ages tweens and up. It’s not super challenging, but again the ones with the common colors on both sides are the most challenging.

This puzzle is Made in China and being sold by a Canadian company on Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: Spin Flip Puzzle - Hypnotic - Spin it, Flip it, Solve it! for Those who Love Brain teasers! Adult Fidget Toy. Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women

It doesn't break unless really forced to. The sprinkles and charm are nice editions and my daughter was surprised that the paper straw released readily from the slime.
The big oversight is that all of the imagery shows off the fun of combining the two colors together. The first problem that causes is one of storage. The two colors come separately packed in small containers with no extra room. This means if you combine them, you have no where to store the combined slime. Also, this should be fairly obvious, but as soon as you start mixing the colors it takes about 5 seconds for the red and white to simply become a pink. You could make the swirl shown in the product photos, but you'd never be able to interact with it without forever just having a pink slime.

Lastly, while the packaging is probably more eco-friendly than most, it is super non-descript. Just a brown box with a couple of tube and a small baggy of sprinkles and the charm.
text_fidelity_b: Strawberry Butter Slime for Party Favors, Scented, Soft and Non-Sticky, Birthday Gifts for Girl Boys, Stress Relief Slime

Now you pack up and they all go.... back into the box to need sorting again next time. This stacked tray takes care of that! What a great idea!

We got this with a single puzzle in mind, but now looking at it, we think we might do one half for one puzzle and the other half for another (we’d use sticky notes or scrap paper to remind us which was which.

It’s a great size so you can fit a large number of pieces. You can work them in the tray or on the table - you can have one tray exposed, or pull it apart and have multiple.

CAUTION: Be careful pulling them apart - it is solid and “tight,” but not so tight you can’t get them apart, but enough that if you pull too hard pieces could go flying.

Materials are solid, size is good for on a table, side table, or shelf. And it looks nice. Something you wouldn’t mind having seen in the living room or family room.

Overall we are very happy with this find and happy to recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Sticker Design Studio, Paint & Print Art Activity, Repositionable Stickers, Decorate Gear, School Supplies & More (74-7217) If your kids primarily want this kit because, "cool, I made my own stickers!" then they probably will enjoy it. If, like me, they liked the look of the stickers in the advertising, be warned that's more difficult to achieve. I included some pictures of my finished stickers to give an idea of the type of stickers included.

Update: In the end, I've found it easiest to put the drops of paint directly on the sticker sheet, with the desired colors in the right spots (including a red and yellow drop together to make orange, or two red and one blue to make purple, or two yellow and one blue to make green. The blue is very strong and tends to overwhelm the other colors, so use less of it). THEN I use the roller (included) or a sponge brush (not included) to mix the colors directly on the sticker. The problem with using the mat as directed is that too much paint made the roller not mix well, but too little paint meant that the stickers didn't evenly coat with the paint. There would be bare spots (even if paint was under that area) or the paint was thin in spots.

Original review: The first thing I did when I got this set was open it and read the directions. Knowing that practice makes perfect, I tried my first efforts on some white card stock. I followed the directions about the amount of paint to drop on the mat and how many times to run the roller over those drops. The roller started skidding instead of rotating after two passes, so the paint wasn't mixing in the cool, tie-dye-look way. As I used all three colors, the paint quickly turned into a muddy, grayed color. I put the card stock down on the paint, rubbed on the card stock to transfer the paint, turned it over and used the Pattern Design Tool to scratch some lines into the solid color. Some paint came off, some didn't, so it wasn't a clean plaid-pattern type look. Hmm. I looked at the pictures more closely and realized you use the pattern tool on the paint BEFORE you transfer the paint to the paper. The transfer mat looked so much like the finished notebook that this wasn't as clear as it could have been, and the text didn't mention this information. Ok, so that worked, though it's a little hit-or-miss how nice it'll look.

Next attempt: The paint pattern turned into a variety of greens again rather than a tie-dye look, but I loaded the roller (like the cover of the directions shows) and rolled it over the stencil of the dots. Not one bit of paint got on the card stock below the stencil. I used a sponge-brush to pick up paint and dab it on the card stock through the stencil. That worked, but the sponge brush isn't included in this set. I mixed more paint and I used the roller on the zebra stripes stencil, and just a little got through in the larger portions of the design. I tried flipping the paint-covered stencil and rubbing the paint on the stencil onto the card. That worked pretty well, but it's not quite as nice of a design. Then I realized I'd mixed up the directions. You either press the stencil into the paint on the transfer mat and transfer that to the card stock OR put the stencil on the transfer mat, put the paint on the stencil, then roll it down through the holes in the stencil onto the transfer mat, and finally transfer it to the card stock. The roller is only for mixing the paint.

Next try: I only used yellow and red paint and less of it, and I finally got a pretty yellow, orange, and red tie-dye look. If I put a sticker from the sticker sheet down on the paint and rubbed to transfer the paint, that would be a decent success. But I put the card stock on the paint and rubbed the paint onto the card stock. It looked pretty good, but some spots had less paint than others.

So (1) practice a bit before you do your stickers, (2) use only two colors at a time if you wish to create brighter colors (less gray or brownish areas), and (3) you may be able to use 6-9 drops of paint, but this made the roller just skid for me; fewer drops resulted in better blending. Putting the drops in groups (several drops of the same color next to each other) rather than alternately (blue, then yellow, then red) also resulted in more colorful mixes.

Clean up is easy--simply run the mat and tools under warm water in your sink, then dry with a paper towel. All materials are nontoxic. The paints may stain clothing or furniture, though, so wear protective clothing when working with the paint, cover the work surface while painting, and wash up immediately with warm water when finished.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Sticker Design Studio, Paint & Print Art Activity, Repositionable Stickers, Decorate Gear, School Supplies & More (74-7217)
